_readme: THE NATIVE BRIDGE MANIFEST. What ops/fetch-bridges.mjs downloads to replace
seven of the eight containers the deleted docker-compose.yml once ran.
WHY THIS EXISTS. Docker Desktop on macOS is a Linux virtual machine: several
GB of disk, a gig-plus of resident RAM, a commercial licence for business
use, and an install-time dependency on a product this one does not control.
It was carried because the bridges were believed to need it. They do not.
Every mautrix bridge in this stack is Go and publishes a prebuilt
darwin-arm64 binary; verified 2026-08-29 against the GitHub release API, and
one of them (linkedin) downloaded, checksum-matched and inspected by hand.
PINNED BY SHA256, EVERY ONE. The compose file this replaced pinned its images by
digest but ops/prefetch-bridges.sh pulled discord, slack and linkedin by the
mutable ':latest' tag, so a first launch could warm the cache with different
code than the stack later ran. A manifest of content hashes cannot drift that
way: the sha256 IS the version.
The sums below are upstream's own, read from each release's sha256sums.txt.
Do not hand-edit one. Re-run the release's sha256sums.txt and copy it, or the
check that makes this file worth having is the check you just disabled.
libolm: every one of these binaries links @rpath/libolm.3.dylib, and upstream
does NOT ship that dylib as a release asset (its macOS CI produces it as a
build artifact only). The rpath lists @executable_path first, so the dylib
goes beside the binary. Providing it is a separate leg of this migration --
see ops/fetch-bridges.mjs, which verifies rather than assumes.

bridges.note: Messenger. The meta repo ships two binaries; this is the Facebook one.
Instagram. Same repo and release as meta, different binary -- the same two-bridge split bridges/README.md describes.

Ran on a 2026-08-25 dev-build digest under the container engine because released v26.08 could not complete an X login (HTTP 403 behind a Cloudflare challenge). This is the RELEASED build and X logs in on it: confirmed by the owner on 2026-08-30 against this manifest, after the login window stopped advertising WebAuthn it cannot perform. Kept as a note rather than deleted because the failure was real and a future Cloudflare change could bring it back.
Go since the April 2026 rewrite; it was the last Python bridge in this stack. Still needs the owner's own api_id/api_hash before it will start -- that is unchanged and has nothing to do with Docker.

exampleConfig.note: Pre-bridgev2 binaries have no -e/--generate-example-config flag: the CONTAINER shipped example-config.yaml and its entrypoint copied it in, so `docker run` bare produced a config and the bare binary produces `failed to read config: no such file`. Fetched from the source tree at the same pinned tag as the binary, and hashed like everything else here.

bridges.note: Still pre-bridgev2, hence the different version line and the exampleConfig above. Was pulled by ':latest' before this file existed.
The binary this migration was proved against: downloaded 2026-08-29, sha256 matched upstream, Mach-O arm64, Signature=adhoc (linker-signed), links @rpath/libolm.3.dylib.
Was pulled by ':latest' before this file existed.
